en: The Philippines is an archipelago consisting of exactly 7,641 islands, with only about 2,000 of them being large enough to be inhabited.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape and has erupted over 50 times in the last 400 years.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Babuyan Channel.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers across Laguna and Rizal.
The Philippine tarsier is one of the world's smallest primates, measuring only 85 to 160 millimeters in height and weighing up to 160 grams.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer-long underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones each year, with the typhoon season typically peaking between the months of July and October.
The Philippines produces about 10 percent of the world's total nickel supply, making it one of the top global exporters of nickel ore.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares of pristine marine habitat in the Sulu Sea, protecting over 600 species of fish.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching approximately 425 kilometers northeast to southwest between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan City drops 98 meters in two cascades, generating about 70 percent of the hydroelectric power for Mindanao.
